title: AMIs, snapshots and building an image of your own

videos.script: Every instance starts from an image, and most people never look at one. This lesson opens one up. {{record}} An AMI is not a file. It is a short record that describes a machine, and points at snapshots that hold the bytes. You will read a real record, and find the current image by a name that never changes. {{snapshots}} Then the snapshots themselves. The first one stores everything written. The next stores only what changed. That is why thirty nightly copies cost a fraction of thirty full ones, and you will do the arithmetic with AWS's price. {{build}} Next you build an image of your own. You launch an instance, configure it, and save it. Every machine launched from it starts with the same bytes. {{share}} Then the life after. An image is copied to other regions, shared with other accounts, and marked old when a newer one arrives. {{retire}} And at the end it is retired. That step is easy to get half right. Remove the image and its snapshot stays behind, billed every month, for nothing anybody can launch.
